newsitem.title: FINLAND: EQUITY DERIVATIVES ONLY SLIGHTLY NERVOUS - BROKERS.
newsitem.headline: EQUITY DERIVATIVES ONLY SLIGHTLY NERVOUS - BROKERS.

text.p: Derivatives markets have shown only slight nervousness as the stock market rocketed to new highs in the first weeks of the year amid some fears a current bull-run may be near its end, options brokers said on Friday.
Implied volatilities have risen somewhat, particularly on puts, and the FOX future is trading below its theoretical value but levels are still normal, they said.
"There is nothing alarming in the market, at least not yet," one broker said.
According to Finnish derivatives exchange SOM, the weighted average implied volatility on the February options at Friday's close was 22.65 percent compared to 22.45 at end-1996.
Average April volatility was 21.41 percent, up from 20.25 at the end of last year. Historical 10-day volatility was 16.78 percent.
The February FOX future closed clearly below its 932.85 theoretical value at 922.75, with the index at 929.77.
"The situation is not exceptional," one broker said.
One said outright put buying was becoming more active, explaining the higher volatilities, and that cylinder strategies locking both the up- and downsides were also used.
Another broker said activity in December was more bearish than it has been in January.
